title: SQL Injection - Authentication Bypass (Admin Login)
impact: An unauthenticated attacker can log in as any account, including the administrator, without knowing the password, gaining full control of the shop and its user data.
remediation: Build the login query with parameterized/prepared statements (or an ORM with bound parameters) instead of concatenating email and password into SQL, and reject unexpected input.

title: SQL Injection - UNION-Based Data Extraction (Product Search)
payload_used: ')) UNION SELECT id, email, password, '1','2','3','4','5','6' FROM Users--
impact: An unauthenticated attacker can append a UNION SELECT to the search query and dump every user's email address and MD5 password hash, enabling account takeover through offline cracking.
remediation: Use parameterized queries for the search term and never concatenate user input into SQL; restrict database privileges and store passwords with a slow hash such as bcrypt or Argon2.

title: Reflected XSS - Script Execution via Product Search
impact: An attacker can send a crafted link that executes arbitrary JavaScript in a victim's browser in the shop's origin, enabling session theft, phishing, or actions performed as the victim.
remediation: HTML-encode the search term before inserting it into the DOM, avoid rendering untrusted input as HTML, and enforce a Content-Security-Policy that disallows javascript: URLs and inline frames.

title: Stored XSS - Payload Persisted in User Email (Admin User List)
impact: The payload is saved in the database and executes in the administrator's browser whenever the Administration page is loaded, letting an attacker perform admin actions or steal the admin session.
remediation: Validate the email format on the server instead of relying on client-side validation, HTML-encode untrusted values instead of rendering them via innerHTML/bypassSecurityTrustHtml, and apply a strict Content-Security-Policy.
